_about: Shared cases for the sensitivity-declaration parity check. This file is the ONE
source of cases for both readers of a sensitivity declaration: the compiler's
reader over a compiled schema, and this plugin's reader over the authored entity
JSON it receives. Both sides enumerate this file, so a case added here is checked
on both sides and a case removed from here fails the compiler-side check's
shape-class census. Add a case HERE rather than inline in either reader's own
unit tests, or the two sides stop being compared on it.
Every `schema` value is an entity's authored spec.schema, written in JSON because
that is the form the plugin receives (the host converts the entity YAML to JSON
before invoking a rule) and because JSON is valid YAML, so the compiler side
`expect` is the compiler-side truth: the flat-dotted leaf paths, per pillar, that
the compiler reads as declared sensitive. An omitted pillar means the empty set.
`guestBlindPaths` names paths the plugin-side reader cannot reach because the
declaration is nested inside a YAML text block that only a YAML parser can open.
The plugin has no YAML parser, so the divergence is real and is recorded here
rather than hidden: the plugin side asserts it collects `expect` MINUS these, and
that it reports exactly these as unreadable.

leafCases.name: typeless-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: A leaf carrying only the marker is a leaf, not an object with a property named sensitive.

leafCases.name: typed-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: The ordinary shape: a marker beside a type.

leafCases.name: sibling-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: A marker on one leaf must not spread to its siblings.

leafCases.name: pillars-are-independent
leafCases.why: A path is unique only within its pillar, so the same name may differ across pillars.

leafCases.name: nested-implicit-object
leafCases.why: Nesting expressed by YAML hierarchy alone; the collected path is the dotted chain.

leafCases.name: nested-explicit-properties
leafCases.why: Nesting expressed with an authored properties map; `properties` is a keyword, not a leaf name.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-ref
leafCases.why: A marker beside a reference is carried onto the referring node.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-allof
leafCases.why: A marker beside a composition keyword is carried onto the composing node.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-anyof
leafCases.why: Same as allOf; each composition keyword takes the same path.

leafCases.name: marker-beside-oneof
leafCases.why: Same as allOf; each composition keyword takes the same path.

leafCases.name: composition-branch-leaf-declares-on-the-composing-node
leafCases.why: A branch composes onto the object carrying it, so a marker on the branch itself declares the carrying property.

leafCases.name: composition-branch-properties-declare-below-the-composing-node
leafCases.why: A branch's own property map contributes below the carrying property's path, never below the branch.

leafCases.name: conditional-branch-properties-declare-below-the-carrying-node
leafCases.why: The single-schema composition keywords compose the same way as the list-valued ones, so a marker under one of them declares too.

leafCases.name: negated-branch-leaf-declares-on-the-carrying-node
leafCases.why: A negated branch describes a shape an instance must avoid, so reading a marker there can only withhold a datum that could never validate.

leafCases.name: reference-target-declares-at-the-referring-path
leafCases.why: A definitions block authored beside the properties that use it resolves there, and the declaration lands at the referring property's path plus its own chain — no authored datum lives inside the definition.

leafCases.name: reference-target-at-the-document-root-resolves-too
leafCases.why: A definitions block authored at the document root is a reference scope as well, so the same pointer resolves from an outer scope.

leafCases.name: recursive-reference-declaring-terminates-and-withholds-the-tail
leafCases.why: A target that reaches itself cannot be enumerated further, so the referring path is collected when the recursion carries a declaration anywhere.

leafCases.name: recursive-reference-declaring-nothing-stays-readable
leafCases.why: A path is sensitive only when an author said so, so a recursive schema carrying no marker must not be withheld by the cycle rule alone.

leafCases.name: unresolvable-reference-collects-the-referring-path
leafCases.why: What an unresolvable target declares is unknown, so naming the referring property is the most precise declaration available and the only one that cannot under-report. The property map beside the reference still yields no reachable leaf on either side.

leafCases.name: composition-sibling-properties-are-not-walked
leafCases.why: A property map beside a composition keyword yields no reachable leaf on either side.

leafCases.name: array-items-are-not-walked
leafCases.why: A marker on an array's element type is not a leaf of the enclosing object.

leafCases.name: object-marker-and-nested-marker
leafCases.why: An object may declare the marker itself and still carry declaring children.

leafCases.name: only-boolean-true-declares
leafCases.why: A composed schema records which entity declared a keyword under the same keyword spelling, mapped to an entity name; a presence-only read would take that for a declaration.

leafCases.name: explicit-jsonschema-mode-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: Under an explicit JSON Schema mode the key is authored JSON Schema content, not the compact-form marker.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-declares-nothing-at-its-own-node
leafCases.why: An escaped body is embedded as authored JSON Schema, so its own key is not the marker.

leafCases.name: escape-mapping-body-nested-leaf-declares
leafCases.why: Children inside an escaped body are dispatched normally, so a nested compact leaf still declares.

leafCases.name: escape-text-body-is-unreadable-in-the-guest
leafCases.why: A YAML text block needs a YAML parser to open; the guest has none, so this divergence is declared rather than hidden.

leafCases.name: pillar-root-as-a-leaf-declares-nothing
leafCases.why: A pillar whose own node reads as a leaf exposes no properties, so nothing is collected — the shape an author hits when naming a property `sensitive`.

leafCases.name: nothing-declared
leafCases.why: The silent half: a schema with no marker anywhere collects nothing.

leafCases.name: pillar-outside-the-axis
leafCases.why: The axis covers values, infra and provides only.

leafCases.name: empty-schema
leafCases.why: An entity with no schema content declares nothing.

slotCases.name: slot-marker-quoted-string
slotCases.why: A non-boolean is not a declaration on either side; the compiler additionally refuses to decode it.

slotCases.name: slot-marker-number
slotCases.why: As above: the marker is boolean-only.
